WRITING IN BAC EXAMS

I-GUIDED WRITING: (4MKS):

1-A PARAGRAPH         2-A BIOGRAPHY         3-AN ADVERTISEMENT

II-FREE WRITING: (8MKS):

 1-AN ARTICLE             2-A LETTER                 3-A SPEECH

III-HOW TO WRITE A ...... ? :

A 

paragraph

:

Topic sentence : One-sentence introduction 

Supporting

details

 : Arguments/ Events/

Reasons….

. 

Linkers of addition: Moreover / Furthermore / In addition / Besides / What's more 

Linkers of contrast

: .

 but, yet, while, whereas, in spite of, despite, Although, however, Nevertheless, even so, on the one hand, on the other hand, on the contrary

Linkers of 

succession:

 - First of all / Firstly / To begin with / First …. - Second / Secondly / Then … - Third / Thirdly / After that... - The next stage … 

Conclusion sentence : One sentence-conclusion - Finally / in short / to sum up / in conclusion / lastly / last but not least…

present

 tense in argumentative paragraphs

An 

advertisement

title

* 

reason

: to 

convince

 (to persuade) (to donate/ to participate in an event/ to buy a product/ to go on a trip or package holiday/ to enroll in a virtual school....) 

* Use of positive adjectives 

* Use of superlative (the best, the most exciting....) 

* H

ighlight

 the benefits of the donation, the package tour, the event, the virtual school....

* Use the simple 

present

 tense

A 

biography

 :

* Use the simple past tense

* (Name of the person) was born on (2nd of April) in (year) in (country). S/he + verb (simple past tense), then (worked for 3 years in…). (Five) years later, s/he … In 1987, s/he was awarded (the Nobel Prize). At the age of 62, he died (=passed away)

A 

letter

 :

Dear ……………, 

I am writing this letter to you to (reasons for writing: ask for, thank you, complain about, encourage you

Body of the letter: use linkers to introduce your ideas/ arguments First, ………

…./

I am looking forward to (+ 

verb

 + 

ing

)to

 hearing from you soon to dealing with your agency again to getting compensation

                                                                                                        Yours,

 name)

An article :

Introduction: 

A: general introduction

* 

definition

 of the phenomenon 

* 

compare

 something with another 

* 

the

 present vs the past 

* you notice the spread of something in society nowadays (attitude, 

behavior,…

)

B: thesis statement 

(Classify the arguments) {emotional, financial, physical, medical, ethical, social, personal, aesthetics, entertaining, professional, voluntary, non-voluntary….} {advantages + disadvantages} 

Body paragraphs: Every paragraph (topic sentence +supporting details (linkers) + concluding sentence)

Conclusion: To conclude, ......To 

summarize,...

..Briefly,........

A speech :

There are many kinds of speeches, including those intended to inform, persuade, instruct, motivate, and entertain. They all share the same goal, however: to communicate clearly and effectively to an audience. 

Adress

:

 the audience (Ladies and Gentlemen/ Dear classmates/pupils………………..) 

Catch:the

 attention of the audience (joke/ statistics/ anecdote/ proverb…)

Tell your audience about the out line of your speech.

Conclude 

briefly
